title: Lodges That Help
bigQuestion: How can a club help its members and its neighbors?

story.title: Help Comes to the Door
story.kicker: Papa is too sick to work. Who will help the family now?
paragraphs: Long ago, about 120 years ago, Rosa lives in Chicago. Her family has a small home on a busy street. Papa works hard every day. But one winter, Papa gets very sick. He has to stay in bed. (Rosa is made up, but families like hers were real.)
Mama looks worried. With no work, there is no pay. How will they buy food? How will they pay the doctor? Rosa sits by the window and watches the snow.
Then someone knocks. It is Mr. Cole from Papa's lodge. Papa is a member of this club. Mr. Cole brings money from the lodge. He says, "We help each other. The lodge doctor will come tomorrow."
Each week, the lodge brings help until Papa is well. When spring comes, Papa goes back to work. He tells Rosa, "Now I will help the next family." Rosa smiles. That is what good neighbors do.
story.think: How did the lodge help Rosa's family? Who helps your family when things are hard?

lessons.title: From Builders to Clubs
lessons.mainIdea: Later, many clubs called lodges formed so members could help each other.
reading: Remember the builders' hut called a lodge? Later, the word *lodge* came to mean a club, too. Many members were not builders at all.
Some lodge clubs are the Freemasons, the Odd Fellows and the Moose. Members met in a lodge room. They became friends.
A big idea for many lodges was helping. Each *member* paid a little money. When a member needed help, the lodge used that money.

words.d: a club, or the room where its members meet
a person who belongs to a club or group

look.title: A Jar for Helping
look.text: Look at the big glass jar on the lodge table. Each member drops in one coin every week. The jar fills up slowly. One day, a member cannot work. The lodge takes coins from the jar to help him.
look.prompt: Why is it good that everyone puts in a little? What could your class save up for together?

check.q: What did the word lodge come to mean later?
choices: A club, or the room where it meets
check.why: Later, the word lodge came to mean a club and its meeting room.

check.q: What is a member?
choices: A person who belongs to a club
check.why: A member is a person who belongs to a club or group.

check.q: How did many lodges save money to help?
check.why: Each member paid a little money. The lodge used it when a member needed help.

lessons.title: Help When Someone Is Sick
lessons.mainIdea: Many lodges paid for doctors and gave money when a member was too sick to work.
reading: Long ago, a sick worker got no pay. His family could go hungry. That was scary for many families.
Many lodges had a *lodge doctor*. The doctor visited sick members. The lodge helped pay the cost.
Many lodges also gave sick members money each week. That is what Mr. Cole brought to Rosa's family. It helped until Papa was well.

words.d: a doctor who cared for the members of a lodge

look.title: The Doctor's Visit
look.text: Look at the doctor at the door. He holds a black bag. He smiles at Rosa. He walks to Papa's bed and listens to his heart. Mama does not have to pay him today. The lodge will help.
look.prompt: How do you think Rosa feels when the doctor comes? Why?

check.q: Why was it hard when a worker got sick long ago?
choices: He had to build a church
check.why: Long ago, a sick worker got no pay, and his family could go hungry.

check.q: Who is a lodge doctor?
choices: A doctor who cared for lodge members
check.why: A lodge doctor visited and cared for the members of a lodge.

check.q: What did Mr. Cole bring to Rosa's family?
check.why: Mr. Cole brought money from the lodge to help while Papa was sick.

lessons.title: Help for Widows and Children
lessons.mainIdea: Many lodges helped widows and children when a member died.
reading: Sometimes a member died. His wife was then a *widow*. She had to care for the children alone. Many lodges helped her with money.
Lodges also helped pay for the funeral. A funeral is a time when people gather to say goodbye.
Some lodges helped children whose mom or dad had died. The Moose club built a whole town for children in Illinois. It is called Mooseheart. It opened in 1913.

words.d: a woman whose husband has died
a time when people gather to say goodbye to someone who died

look.title: A Town for Children
look.text: Look at the town on the farm near Batavia, Illinois. There are homes, a school and a big green field. Children walk to class together. Grown-ups there help care for them. The Moose club members pay to keep it going.
look.prompt: What would a child need in a town like this? Name three things.

check.q: What is a widow?
choices: A woman whose husband has died
check.why: A widow is a woman whose husband has died.

check.q: Which club built Mooseheart, a town for children?
check.why: The Moose club built Mooseheart in Illinois. It opened in 1913.

check.q: What is a funeral?
choices: A time to say goodbye to someone who died
check.why: A funeral is a time when people gather to say goodbye.

lessons.title: People Helping People
lessons.mainIdea: Many different groups started their own lodges so their families could get help too.
reading: Long ago, some lodges would not let everyone join. Black families were often kept out. Many Catholic families had their own rules about joining.
So people started their own lodges. Black Americans built Prince Hall lodges. Chicago had one by 1852. Catholic men started the *Knights of Columbus* in 1882.
These lodges helped widows, sick members and neighbors, too. People helping people made whole neighborhoods stronger.

words.d: a club for Catholic men, started in 1882, that helps families
a person who lives near you

check.q: Which club did Catholic men start in 1882?

lessons.title: The Shriners Build Hospitals
lessons.mainIdea: A club called the Shriners built hospitals to care for children.
reading: The *Shriners* are a club. Freemasons started the Shriners club. Shriners often wear a red hat called a fez in parades.
About 100 years ago, the Shriners wanted to help children. They built a *hospital* just for children. The first one opened in 1922, in Shreveport, Louisiana.
Children came to get help with bones and walking. Children got care even if their families could not pay.

words.d: a club, started by Freemasons, known for building children's hospitals
a place where doctors and nurses care for people who are sick or hurt

look.title: A Parade With Red Hats
look.text: Look at the parade on the street. A group of men walk by. Each wears a small red hat with a black tassel. Some drive tiny cars. A sign they carry says they help children's hospitals.
look.prompt: What club is this? What does the sign tell you about what they do?

check.q: What did the Shriners build?
check.why: The Shriners built hospitals to care for children.

check.q: Where did the first Shriners hospital open in 1922?
check.why: The first Shriners hospital opened in Shreveport, Louisiana, in 1922.

check.q: What is a hospital?
choices: A place where doctors care for sick or hurt people
A hut at a building site
check.why: A hospital is where doctors and nurses care for people who are sick or hurt.

lessons.title: A Hospital in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1926, the Shriners opened a children's hospital in Chicago.
reading: The Shriners in Chicago met in a big building called Medinah Temple. They wanted a hospital in their city, too.
In 1926, they opened a Shriners hospital in Chicago. It was the 11th Shriners hospital. It helped many children walk and play.
Chicago still has a Shriners hospital for children today. Nurses, doctors and helpers work there every day.

words.d: a person trained to care for people who are sick or hurt

look.title: The Chicago Hospital Opens
look.text: The Shriners hospital in Chicago opened on March 20, 1926. It was the 11th Shriners hospital. Shriners from Medinah Temple helped build it.
look.cite: Shriners Children's Chicago, Our History (hospital website)
look.prompt: What year did the Chicago hospital open? Who helped build it?

check.q: When did the Shriners open a hospital in Chicago?
check.why: The Chicago Shriners hospital opened in 1926.

check.q: Where did the Chicago Shriners meet?
check.why: The Chicago Shriners met in a big building called Medinah Temple.

check.q: Which Shriners hospital was the Chicago one?
check.why: The Chicago hospital was the 11th Shriners hospital.

lessons.title: A Very Tall Temple
lessons.mainIdea: In 1892, Chicago's Masonic Temple was one of the tallest buildings in the world.
reading: In 1892, a new building went up in Chicago. It stood at State Street and Randolph Street. It was called the *Masonic Temple*.
It had more than 20 floors. That was very tall long ago! It was one of the tallest buildings in the world. Shops were at the bottom. Lodge rooms were at the top.
The building is gone now. It was torn down in 1939. But people still remember it in old pictures.

words.d: a tall Chicago building from 1892 with lodge rooms at the top
one level of a building; also called a story

look.title: How Many Floors?
look.cite: The Skyscraper Museum, Tallest Towers: Masonic Temple; Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat
look.prompt: Which building has the most floors? How many more floors did the Masonic Temple have than the Home Insurance Building?

check.why: The Masonic Temple went up in Chicago in 1892.

check.q: What was at the top of the Masonic Temple?
check.why: Shops were at the bottom. Lodge rooms were at the top.

check.q: What happened to the Masonic Temple in 1939?
check.why: The building was torn down in 1939.

lessons.title: Kind Clubs Welcome Questions
lessons.mainIdea: A kind club is happy to answer your questions about what it does.
reading: Ava wants to join a club. She asks, "What do you do?" The leader smiles. "We help at the food bank," she says. "Ask us anything."
A kind club likes every *question* you ask. It tells you what it does. It is happy for your family to know, too.
A club may have a fun password. That is fine. But no one should ask you to hide something that hurts. Tell a trusted grown-up.

words.d: something you ask to find out more
an adult who listens to you and helps keep you safe

look.title: Two Clubs
look.text: Look at two clubs. The first club says, "We clean the park. Bring your mom or dad to see!" The second club says, "Don't tell your family about us. It is a secret."
look.prompt: Which club acts like a kind club? What would you do if a club said the second thing?

check.q: What does a kind club do when you ask questions?
check.why: A kind club likes questions and tells you what it does.

check.q: Someone says, "Hide this from your family. It hurts." What do you do?
check.why: No one should ask you to hide something that hurts. Tell a trusted grown-up.

check.q: What did Ava's club do?
check.why: The leader said her club helps at the food bank.
